newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia pipeline seen pumping again in 24 hours.
newsitem.headline: Colombia pipeline seen pumping again in 24 hours.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol said engineers started repairing the country's main oil pipeline Wednesday afternoon following a leftist rebel dynamite attack over the weekend and that work would take 24 hours.

The Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline serves Occidental Petroleum Corp's field in eastern Arauca province and a company spokesman said production there would be halted if repairs were not completed by "about" midnight local time (0500 GMT Thursday).
"In 24 hours the pipeline will be pumping again...about this time tomorrow," an Ecopetrol spokesman told Reuters.

An Occidental spokesman, meanwhile, said that wells had been shut and production had already been scaled back at its Cano Limon field. If repairs were not completed by midnight, production would have to be halted completely, he said.

"It's possible repairs could take longer. Our deadline is midnight but that could be extended to the early hours," he said. When asked if that meant production would shut down after that time if repairs were not completed, he replied "yes".

The 300,000 barrels per day capacity pipeline was blasted by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels Sunday. The guerrillas later shot down a helicopter transporting troops into the area, killing 20 soldiers and a civilian pilot.
An Ecopetrol spokesman said the quantity of crude spilled could only be determined once pumping restarted.

Sunday's pipeline blast was the sixth in just one month and the 36th in the year. Occidental has cut output from a daily average of about 180,000 bpd to 171,000 bpd over the last month because of the attacks.
Ecopetrol said at least one million barrels of production had been lost from Cano Limon in the year so far because of the pipeline explosions.
